label: Glassflow
Window buttons
Enable macOS-style traffic lights *Replaces the window controls with round glass buttons. Turn OFF Arc 2.0's own 'macOS style buttons' first, or the two mods fight over layout.*
Position *Which end of the sidebar row the buttons sit on. Set explicitly, so this does not depend on zen.view.experimental-force-window-controls-left.*
Show colour at rest *On: buttons are always tinted. Off: neutral grey until you hover the group, which is how Arc behaves.*
Stretch into vertical ovals on hover *Buttons grow taller and lose their perfect circle when the group is hovered. Height animates, so nothing around them reflows.*
Show glyphs on hover *Fades in the close, minimise and maximise marks when the group is hovered.*
Close colour *Purple by default: destructive, but softer than red. Any CSS colour works. Alpha below 1 is what makes it read as glass rather than paint.*
Minimise colour *Blue by default, which reads as 'send away'. Keep the alpha below about 0.7 or the glass effect disappears.*
Maximise colour *Green by default, the one colour macOS already uses for zoom. Keep the alpha below about 0.7.*
Diameter *Resting size. macOS uses 12px, Arc uses 14px. The hover oval is 1.55x this height.*
Gap between buttons *Horizontal spacing. macOS uses roughly 8px.*
Glassy tabs
Enable glassy workspace-tinted tabs *Tints tabs with the current workspace colour. Painted as a background-image so it stacks above Arc's tab colours instead of fighting them.*

Selected tab tint *How much workspace colour the active tab carries. Keep this well above the unselected value or the two states stop being distinguishable at a glance. Try 20% for subtle, 60% for bold.*
Unselected tab tint *Background tabs. Above roughly 20% these start competing with the selected tab. If you want subtle tints everywhere, turn on the accent bar instead.*
Hover tint *Applied to background tabs under the cursor. Sits between the unselected and selected values.*
Gradient direction *How the workspace colour fades across the selected tab. Left-to-right reads as depth, top-to-bottom as sheen.*
Frosted blur *A compositor pass per tab, and the most expensive option here. Turn this off first if scrolling feels heavy, or if you already run several transparency mods and tabs look muddy.*
Blur strength *Only applies when frosted blur is on. Large values smear high-contrast content behind the tab into visible streaks.*
Glass rim *A 1px inner highlight along the top edge. This is the difference between 'glassy' and 'just translucent' -- translucency on its own tends to read as washed out.*
Soft outer glow on the selected tab *Adds a workspace-tinted halo. Replaces the rim's shadow, so it includes the rim highlight when both are on.*
Accent bar on the selected tab *A 3px workspace-coloured bar down the left edge. The clearest at-a-glance marker if you prefer to keep tints subtle.*
Troubleshooting

Outline every element Glassflow touches *Magenta dashed outline on tabs, cyan on window buttons. If something you expected to change has no outline, Glassflow is not matching it and the styling comes from another mod.*
